subject: botany
question_text: What is the basic unit of classification? Define it.

verification.note: Chapter 1 (The Living World) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, book p.3 (VSAQ 5 of 9), which prints the question and a model answer but no star ranks and no year citations. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this chapter; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. The 1+1 mark split is a claim until a TS IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The basic unit
lines: Species is the basic unit (lowest category)
steps.why: Classification is a hierarchy of categories, and species is the lowest category in it — every organism is placed in some species first.
common_mistakes: Writing genus or kingdom as the basic unit. The hierarchy starts at species; kingdom is the highest.
Writing 'specie'. The word is species, in both singular and plural.
steps.memory_tip: The ladder of categories ends at species — lowest step, basic unit.
steps.margin_note: Name the unit in the first line so the mark is visible at a glance.

steps.label: Definition of species
lines: A species is a group of individual organisms
steps.why: This is the NCERT definition — the members of one species share fundamental (basic) similarities and can be told apart from the members of other, closely related species.
common_mistakes: Defining species only by interbreeding. For this chapter, write the NCERT wording: fundamental similarities.
Writing 'similar organisms' without 'fundamental'. The marked phrase is fundamental similarities.
steps.memory_tip: Species and Similarities both start with S — a species is a group with fundamental similarities.
steps.margin_note: Write the definition in the NCERT words; one sentence is enough.

insider_note: One mark is for the word species and one for the definition — students who define well but never write 'species' lose the first mark.
